title: A Word Now Crawls the Frame, Not a Chip | vitalii.no
description:
On a shared family kiosk calendar, a PE or swimming lesson got its own small chip, stacked in the same cramped space as homework and real school events. On a busy day, the one reminder that actually mattered — pack your kit — could get crowded out or buried entirely.

KioskFrame.tsx's kit-day matcher was loosened to check only the lesson's leading word, and the event dropped from its own chip down to a simple solid or tinted color. A new PerimeterWord component measures the day cell, builds an SVG textPath that follows the cell's own perimeter, and repeats the word a whole number of times so the loop has no visible seam — scrolling continuously at a fixed speed instead of sitting still as another chip.

The lesson no longer occupies its own row in the cell at all. It only frames whichever events are already there, so a PE or swimming day keeps its full chip space for homework and real events, while the kit reminder still can't be missed.
